chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'Can I pray in the black cap?' He said, 'Do not pray in it, for it is the apparel of the people of the Fire.'

key_terms.السَّوْدَاءِ: The black (one), specifying the color of the cap.
key_terms.الْقَلَنْسُوَةِ: A type of cap or skullcap, often referring to a specific style worn in the region.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray wearing a black cap according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against praying in the black cap (*qalansawah*), identifying it as the distinctive attire of the 'people of Hellfire.' This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khushu'* (devotion) and the symbolic weight of clothing, where specific garments can carry connotations of arrogance or distinctiveness that may distract from the spiritual focus of prayer.
